response: No, computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen is not always necessary for blunt trauma in intoxicated patients. According to the available data, the incidence of abdominal injury in intoxicated, hemodynamically stable, blunt trauma patients with a normal abdominal examination and normal mentation is low. Therefore, physical examination and attention to clinical risk factors can allow for accurate abdominal evaluation without the need for CT scans. This approach can help minimize unnecessary radiation exposure and reduce healthcare costs.
